brief:
An Israeli-made documentary confronting the military operations in Gaza has garnered significant international attention after its screening at a major film festival, Al Jazeera English reported. The film, titled NAZA, received a 25-minute standing ovation at the Biennale, marking an unusual moment for Israeli cinema engaging directly with the conflict.

The extended applause underscores growing momentum around the work among international film audiences and critics. The 25-minute duration of the ovation signals the documentary's resonance with viewers at one of the world's most prestigious film events. The film's reception reflects broader conversations within Israeli society about the country's conduct in Gaza.
dek: A 25-minute standing ovation at the Biennale has put NAZA, an Israeli-made film confronting Israel’s genocide in Gaza.
title: Israeli documentary on Gaza receives standing ovation at Venice Biennale
